brief: The Market Ear compiles evidence for and against an AI inflection. AI adoption keeps growing but is decelerating, and the token mix is shifting away from frontier models. Top-1% AI customer spending, which drives most enterprise model-company revenue, fell 9.7% last month, from $7,976 to $7,205. Anthropic's S-1 has slipped from early to late September, pushing IPO marketing to mid-October and delaying investor visibility into GAAP revenue and costs behind its roughly $2 trillion rumored valuation, which the note says now needs heroic 2028-and-beyond assumptions. OpenAI's IPO has also slipped, with 2026 called wishful thinking and 2027 the more plausible window. Hedge fund positioning in AI has washed out: the Broad AI long/short ratio sits at the 38th percentile versus its 1-year high, AI Power exposure is near 1-year lows, and general tech allocations have fallen from five-year highs. Mutual funds remain underweight AI. Despite all this, AI infrastructure EPS growth is still outpacing the rest of the market, so the note stops short of calling the inflection.
